messages:
ryan: Heads-up — starting ~09:14 UTC EU pool showed token drain + queue depth spike, latency creeping up. p99 token-grab time went from 12ms -> 180ms. :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] eu-west1: admission_queue_depth>500 (5m avg), token_refill_rate dropped 35%.
marta: saw that too. a bunch of small requests from a single org spiking admission. looks like per-customer accounting skewed somehow.
alex: any KV timeouts in the logs? slowed token ledger writes could cause apparent "leak" because refill not applied.
sasha: yes, I see intermittent 502s in ledger writes to redis-proxy (eu-west1). p50 ok, p95/99 are spiking. network team flagged a backend NAT gateway issue earlier.
ryan: thanks. hypothesis: slow KV causes tokens to be considered in-flight longer -> admission admits fewer new requests -> queue backs up -> token accounting looks like negative refill (we smear credits but backlog grows).
ops-oncall: for immediate mitigation can we do two things: 1) emergency per-customer cap 2) lower global burst window to free headroom?
alex: agreed. quick patch suggestion — apply weighted per-customer cap with emergency_scale. patch snippet:```
def admit(customer, base_tpm, active_sessions, emergency_scale=0.7):
    weight = max(0.1, 1.0 / (1 + active_sessions/10))
    allowed_tpm = int(base_tpm * weight * emergency_scale)
    return allowed_tpm
```
marta: nice. that keeps some fairness while shedding load. can we also reduce token smear window from 30s -> 5s while we investigate so old pending tokens don't mask current shortage?
sasha: we can flip smear window via config flag. doing that will make refill more reactive to current capacity but might increase burstiness if upstream recovers.
jen: callout: if we keep emergency_scale low for >1h we should estimate cost delta for cross-region fallback. shifting 20% of traffic to dedicated fallback GPUs will cost ~$X/hr, FYI to finance.
ops-oncall: scheduler note: enable regional fallback routing for non-enterprise customers first (less SLA constraints) — avoids breaking paid tenants.
ryan: rolling plan: 1) apply per-cust cap + emergency_scale=0.65 2) reduce smear window to 5s 3) enable routing fallback for non-enterprise 4) monitor token-ledger success rate and queue depth. if no improvement in 10m, start throttling lowest-priority routes.
alex: added quick PR for cap + config toggle, will deploy to canary in 2m. logs will include `admit_reason` tag so we can count how many requests hit emergency caps.
marta: follow-up: capture per-customer token delta histogram for last 15m to see if any accounts are anomalous (to contact them).
sasha: creating temporary alert: ledger_timeout_rate > 1% -> page infra-oncall.
infra-bot: [ACTION] canary deploy started by alex (deploy/infra-admit-patch) :rocket:
ops-oncall: monitoring — queue depth halved after canary. p95 token-grab down to ~45ms. still seeing some 502s to redis-proxy but much lower.
ryan: great. after stabilizing we'll do a postmortem to fix NAT gateway and add KV client-side circuit-breaker + local token cache to reduce dependency on a single proxy.
jen: please add a short estimate for cost of permanent fallback capacity vs fixing NAT (one-off infra fix). finance wants numbers before next week. :memo:
marta: will generate per-customer impact report and simple cost delta by EOD.
ryan: thanks all. keeping thread open until we revert smear window and emergency_scale to normal. :thumbsup:
